weder.et: From Old High German wedar, from Proto-West Germanic *hwaþar, from Proto-Germanic *hwaþeraz; cognate with English whether and either.

wedeln.et: Either from Middle High German wadelen, wedelen, from Old High German wadalōn or from the noun Wedel.

s: neither fish nor fowl, neither fish nor flesh (something difficult to categorise)

weder Fisch noch Fleisch.et: Literally, “neither fish nor meat”. Compare with Dutch vlees noch vis, French ni chair ni poisson, Polish ni pies, ni wydra, Russian ни рыба ни мясо (ni ryba ni mjaso), and so on. Perhaps from the context of fasting (on Fridays and during Lent), where fish was…

Wedel.et: Inherited from Middle High German wadel / wedel, from Old High German wadal / wedil, from Proto-West Germanic *waþil (“whisk”).
